findings.title: Dataproc cluster has no idle-delete TTL, so a forgotten cluster runs (and bills) forever
findings.explanation: cluster_config has no lifecycle_config block, so GCP applies no idle_delete_ttl / idle_delete_min_dur. A Dataproc cluster is a standing set of Compute Engine VMs (master + workers); with no idle-shutdown policy, a cluster left idle after a job finishes keeps billing indefinitely until someone notices and deletes it manually. This is the single most common Dataproc cost leak.

findings.title: No staging_bucket/temp_bucket set, so GCP auto-creates an unmanaged GCS bucket outside this module's lifecycle
findings.explanation: cluster_config sets neither staging_bucket nor temp_bucket. When both are omitted, Dataproc auto-provisions a regional bucket per project to hold job dependencies and cluster staging data. That bucket is not declared in this Terraform config at all, so it has no lifecycle_rule, isn't destroyed when the cluster is destroyed, and isn't visible to anyone reviewing this module's resource list or cost allocation.
findings.remediation: Accept staging_bucket/temp_bucket as module inputs pointing at caller-managed, lifecycle-ruled buckets (or provision one alongside the cluster in this module with an explicit lifecycle_rule), so storage cost and retention are visible and controlled in Terraform.

findings.title: Dataproc cluster has no labels for cost allocation or ownership tracking
findings.explanation: No labels block on the cluster. Without labels (team, environment, cost-center, etc.), this cluster's spend can't be attributed in billing reports, and it's harder to identify ownership when triaging idle/orphaned clusters.
findings.remediation: Add a labels input variable and pass it through: labels = var.labels.

suggested_policies.rationale: A Dataproc cluster with no lifecycle_config.idle_delete_ttl has no automatic idle shutdown — the single most common way Dataproc clusters silently run up cost after the job that created them has finished. This is a concrete, unambiguous not_null check with no legitimate reason for every cluster to skip it (a genuinely long-running cluster can still set an explicit, deliberately large TTL, or the check can be suppressed per-resource via holden:ignore).
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_XXX
name: Dataproc clusters should define an idle-delete lifecycle policy
principle: cost
severity: LOW
rationale: |
  A Dataproc cluster with no cluster_config.lifecycle_config.idle_delete_ttl
  (or idle_delete_min_dur) never auto-deletes when idle. Clusters are billed
  for their full VM fleet (master + workers) for as long as they exist, so a
  forgotten cluster after a batch job completes silently accumulates cost
  until someone notices and deletes it manually.
remediation: |
  Add a lifecycle_config block:
    cluster_config {
      lifecycle_config {
        idle_delete_ttl = "1800s"
      }
    }
resources:
  google_dataproc_cluster:
    path: cluster_config.lifecycle_config
    not_null: true
